# Independent audit: support-leaf canonical rigidity and status examples

Audited source:
`candidate 06820524b3e6d141`,
Sections 4--6, together with the cited companion
`candidate 00208e2b45f0da1a`.

Result: PASS. No correction identified. This is an audit of the stated
bounded hypotheses, not a general extremizer classification.

## 1. All-fiber facet-constant neutrality

On a common-normal simplex fiber, the relative cap threshold q_j is
strictly between zero and one. Its trace on a different facet is exactly
the homothetic facet simplex with ratio 1-q_j; its own facet trace is
empty. Thus the neutral constant-velocity equations use the actual
(d-1)-dimensional fractions, not full-fiber d-volume fractions.

Subtracting the equations for facets i and h makes
theta_i(1-q_i(z))^(d-1) independent of i. Each equation has d such terms,
so their common value is beta/d. For d>=2, fixed positive theta makes
q_i(z) independent of z. Equal global cap masses then force equal q_i;
the source threshold sum is exactly one, since that cap family passes
through the actual source. This gives q_i=1/(d+1), beta=Gamma_d and
uniform theta. Finally the actual centroid coordinates are precisely
b_i(z)+r_z/(d+1)=L_i(z), proving the claimed affine centroid graph.

Every step uses a displayed hypothesis. In particular it does not
derive independent facet freedom or one-circuit neutrality from general
local minimality with multiple witnesses. The d>=2 restriction is needed
when recovering thresholds from facet fractions.

## 2. Source-affine and translation companion results

I independently checked the companion proofs quoted in Section 5.
The extreme anchored representation polytopes are finite; their common
strict support margin indeed survives both signs of a sufficiently small
Hausdorff change. Input and target are not the changed base simultaneously,
after the self coefficient has been removed. A single defining-plane tilt
realizes the prescribed affine facet velocity on a simplex.

Facet constants give the preceding equal weighted fractions. Facet first
moments then give sum_(j!=i)q_j(v_j-g_Fi)=0. Affine independence on each
facet forces the q_j there to agree; for d>=2 the different facets force
all thresholds equal. For d=1 the endpoint equations give beta=1/2 but
do not determine the source, as correctly stated.

For translations, cap derivative is S_j(z)u_j.t when continuous normals
are unit. Neutrality yields sum theta_j S_j(z)u_j=0. The one-dimensional
minimal-circuit kernel and theta_j proportional to rho_j/S_j make every
ratio S_j(z)/S_j equal. The all-proper/all-zero conclusion therefore
follows under regularity. No support-facet allocation or multiple-witness
neutrality has been inserted.

## 3. The two exact lower-budget calibrations

For radii (19/20,1,21/20), the middle radius equals the average endpoint
radius, so all canonical midpoint supports are active. The proper
endpoint tilt is -1/10. The relative thresholds are exactly
17/57,1/3,23/63. The squared-sum candidate gives Q=6; the smaller
saturated candidate is 2+(9/2)(19/20)^2>6. The total is 5409/400 and
beta=800/1803<4/9. The largest squared radius441/400 is less than half
the total squared-radius sum,601/400. This verifies all arithmetic and
the intended strict no-heavy comparison. Global criticality is supplied
by the separately proved all-normal formula (19)--(20), which I checked
has precisely these hypotheses and includes endpoint maxima.

For radii (1/5,1,1), midpoint support slack is strict. At tilt -3 the
left trace is strictly full and the right strictly empty, while the
middle trace is proper. Thus Q=109/50, M=459/50 and beta=109/459.
The largest endpoint maximum2 is strictly below Q. The canonical source
facet profile has mean4/9, so an inward signed facet motion has a strictly
negative normalized cover response. The example correctly falsifies
neither neutrality nor a bad-minimum theorem: neutrality is absent here.

The all-normal dependency is essential for the global statements; the
displayed proper/saturated traces alone would not establish them.
